n: So many men will die in war that seven women will beg one man to marry them, offering to provide their own food and clothes, just to avoid the shame of being unmarried and childless. This continues the judgment of Isaiah 3.

f.g: To remove the social disgrace of being unmarried or childless.

n: But then hope: the “branch of the Lord” will be beautiful and glorious for the survivors of Israel. Many see the Branch as a title for the Messiah.
Those who remain in Zion and Jerusalem will be called holy — everyone whose name is recorded among the living.
This will happen after the Lord washes away Zion’s filth and Jerusalem’s bloodguilt by a spirit of judgment and burning — purification by fire.
God will place a cloud by day and fire by night over every home and gathering in Zion, like the pillar that guided Israel in the Exodus. His glory will be their protection.

f.w: a cloud and smoke by day and the shining of a flaming fire by night

n: A tabernacle — a shelter — will give shade from the heat and refuge from storm. Latter-day Saints often apply this to the safety found in Zion and its stakes.
